# Programs whose device memory differs between the SASS and PTX engines
# (suites.sh digest) for a reason that is the program's, not an engine's. Each
# still matches the card on the default engine (SASS). A listed program that
# differs is reported, not failed; one that no longer differs is reported too,
# so it can come off the list. Columns: suite | program | the first kernel
# after which they differ and why.
#
# Taken off after the engines were found to differ from the card (2026-10-05):
#   cuda-samples fp16ScalarProduct  srand(time(NULL)): the two runs, a second
#       apart, uploaded different inputs. The digest runs now pin time()
#       (fixed_time.c), and the engines leave the same memory.
#   hecbench bscan-cuda  __ballot_sync((1u << lane) - 1, p): lane 0's mask is
#       empty, so a card traps ("an illegal instruction was encountered");
#       the PTX engine ran it and the SASS engine ran something else. Both trap
#       now (e2e sync_masks).
hecbench|backprop-cuda|kernel_adjust_weights (launch 1): hidden_delta[0], a float no host code ever sets, is uploaded with the other 16 and never read (the kernel indexes delta[tx + 1]); it holds whatever the heap had, a freed chunk's link under glibc's safe-linking, so it changes from run to run, on one engine as on two
rodinia|streamcluster|kernel_compute_cost (every launch): the Point array's float *coord is a host pointer, uploaded and never dereferenced on the device; ASLR moves it between runs (5 bytes of each 32-byte Point, offsets 9 to 13, are all that differ)
